findings.title: A failed revert can block every retry
findings.body: The branch name `revert-<sha8>` is the same on every attempt (line 970). The cleanup at 974 only deletes the branch when the revert commit fails. If opening the merge request at 983 fails, the branch is left behind with the revert commit on it. The same happens when an earlier revert merge request was closed without merging, because `remove_source_branch` only removes the branch on merge. In both cases the next attempt fails at branch creation (971) with GitLab's "already exists" error, and the app gives no way to clear it. Fix: also delete the branch when opening the merge request fails, or add a suffix to the name when it is already taken.

findings.title: Revert-unavailable message can be wrong
findings.body: This error is raised whenever both `merge_commit_sha` and `squash_commit_sha` are empty (gitLabMergeRequestJson.ts:609). That also covers a fast-forward merge of a single commit, and a merge request that was never merged: the server does not check the state, only the UI does (PullRequestActionsMenu.tsx:442). In those cases "landed as several commits" is false. Something like "GitLab recorded no single commit for this merge request" would be accurate in every case.

contracts.action: Revert a merged GitLab merge request: create a branch, revert the commit onto it, open a merge request
contracts.equivalent_path: disable-auto-merge branch of runMergeRequestAction, which goes straight to api()
contracts.before_after: Like disable-auto-merge, it runs before actionArgs/executeMr and writes through api() with the JSON body on stdin and a Content-Type header.
contracts.visible_effect: Errors are mapped by fail("runAction") in the provider and their detail is passed to the client. On success the web client shows the "Revert … opened" toast.
contracts.failure_mode: Decode failure raises GitLabMergeRequestReadError. No single commit raises GitLabRevertUnavailableError. A failed revert commit deletes the new branch. A failure while opening the merge request leaves the branch behind, so retries fail with a visible error.

summary: This adds a GitLab revert action. It reads the merge request, takes the merge commit (or the squash commit as a fallback), creates a `revert-<sha8>` branch from the target branch, reverts the commit onto it, and opens a merge request. If the revert commit fails, the new branch is deleted. Permission is gated by GitLab's `can_merge`. The wiring follows the existing `disable-auto-merge` path, and errors reach the client through the provider's error mapping. Two "consider" notes: the branch name is the same on every attempt, so a failure while opening the merge request (or an earlier revert merge request closed without merging) leaves a branch that makes every retry fail; and the "landed as several commits" message is also shown in cases where it is false.
